cards.title: Does a horse with an excuse bounce back?
cards.question: After interference, a slow start or racing wide, does it do better next time?
cards.answer: Had an excuse: 202/1404 won next time, -26.5 dollars per $100; No recorded excuse: 1089/8217 won next time, -24.4 dollars per $100. Not proven; no live upgrade.
caveats: Exploratory selected histories, not a random population. Prior comment must pre-date next start. Medical problems are not automatic positive upgrades. No causal claim or live upgrade.
cards.method: Next observed run after an earlier source-dated comment. No same-start comments. 5% commission on winnings. Selected form histories may bias the sample. Research only.

cards.title: Favourites vs roughies, by country
cards.question: Do short-priced horses win more than their price says, and roughies less? Is it different in Australia, the UK and Ireland?
cards.answer: Best group anywhere: GB $25+ at +$1 per $100 after commission. Roughies ($25+): AU -$11, GB +$1, IE -$15 per $100.
cards.verdict_reason: GB $25+: 18,584 runners; profit could be -$15 to $18 per $100. Not enough certainty.

cards.title: Leaders and inside draws on the day
cards.question: When early races at a meeting are won by inside barriers, do later races keep going that way?
cards.answer: Only 63 races logged so far (15 after an inside-draw pattern, 9 won by an inside draw again). Needs a few weeks of data.

cards.title: Our own picks so far
cards.question: Is the bot's $100-a-race tally, or its value bets, beating the bookies yet?
cards.answer: 86 graded bets, -$6 per $100. Need thousands before it means anything.

cards.title: Should we skip short favourites that were backed hard?
cards.question: If the pick was $2 or shorter and had already shortened 20% at selection, would skipping it help?
cards.answer: On 35 later, time-stamped picks, this would skip 0 bets. Imaginary profit: $-638 instead of $-638. Too small to trust; not a live rule.
cards.note: Uses selection price and already-recorded opening price only, never final/SP as an input. Retrospective, small nonrandom sample. No change to locked picks or live filter.

cards.title: Time of day
cards.question: Do favourites do better in early races, the middle of the day or at night meetings?
cards.answer: Best window for favourites: Before noon at +$4 per $100. Differences are small.

cards.title: X tipsters vs the market
cards.question: Do the X tipsters' picks win more than the starting price says?
cards.answer: 121 checkable tips: 54 winners, +$14 per $100 at SP. Far too few to call.

cards.title: Form signals: barrier, first-up, weight, jockeys
cards.question: Do good barriers, horses first-up from a spell, weight drops and hot jockeys/trainers win more than their price says?
cards.answer: Strongest: 'Hot trainer' won 5% more than the price said (7989 runners), but after the bookie's cut it's -$23 per $100. The market already prices most of this in.
cards.note: Prices here are TAB/RA starting prices, which carry a bigger bookie margin than Betfair.
cards.verdict_reason: Hot trainer: 7,989 runners; lost $22.51 per $100 after costs. Even the 95% range is below zero.

cards.title: Horses the money comes for
cards.question: Do horses that firm 20%+ before the jump win more than their final price says? Do drifters win less?
cards.answer: Big firmers won 3% less often than their final price said, and backing them at the final price made -$16 per $100 after commission. Big drifters: -$10 per $100.
cards.note: Movement = final Betfair SP vs average pre-race traded price. You only know the full move at the jump, so this is the best case.
cards.verdict_reason: Firmed 20%+: 30,995 runners; lost $15.59 per $100 after costs. Even the 95% range is below zero.

cards.title: Maidens, handicaps and big fields
cards.question: Are favourites better value in maidens, small fields or big fields?
cards.answer: Best: Handicaps favourites at -$2 per $100 after commission.
cards.verdict_reason: Handicaps: 53,289 runners; lost $2.10 per $100 after costs. Even the 95% range is below zero.

cards.title: Stacking signals together
cards.question: If a horse ticks 3+ boxes (good jockey, good trainer, good barrier, ran well last start, likes the distance), does it beat its price?
cards.answer: Horses ticking 4+ boxes won 5% more than their price said (1185 runners), -$26 per $100 at SP.
cards.verdict_reason: 4+ boxes: 1,185 runners; lost $25.98 per $100 after costs. Even the 95% range is below zero.
